description: Looking for people interested in data science and visualizations.
summary:
Our project is a Pakistan-focused environmental monitoring platform developed to make environmental data more accessible and actionable. It brings together data from multiple sources to track key environmental indicators, including air quality, rainfall, and weather patterns across 8 major Pakistani cities.

Through an interactive dashboard, users can explore historical data, compare environmental conditions between cities, visualize trends, and identify concerning changes. By collecting, processing, and presenting environmental datasets in an easy-to-understand format, this environmental trend detector addresses the challenge of fragmented environmental information and limited public accessibility.

The project is important because Pakistan faces increasing environmental challenges, including air pollution, unpredictable rainfall, and climate variability. It aims to empower citizens, researchers, students, and policymakers with meaningful environmental insights to support greater awareness, informed decision-making, and data-driven environmental planning.
details:
Trend Detector helps people understand how their environment is changing using NASA Earth observation data.

Instead of presenting complex satellite datasets, the platform answers four simple questions:

• What is changing?

• Where is it changing?

• How much is it changing?

• Is the change statistically significant?

For our hackathon project, we focus on air quality and rainfall trends across eight major Pakistani cities: Lahore, Karachi, Islamabad, Peshawar, Quetta, Faisalabad, Multan, and Hyderabad.

Using 20 years of monthly observations (2005–2024), we analyze PM2.5, Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), Tropospheric NO₂, and rainfall data to identify long-term environmental trends. Each trend is tested using established statistical methods including OLS regression, Mann-Kendall trend analysis, and Theil-Sen slope estimation.

The platform includes:

Trend Explorer – Interactive charts and maps that show how environmental conditions have changed over time.

Pollution Index – An exploratory score that combines PM2.5, NO₂, and AOD to help users compare environmental change across cities. It is not an official AQI or health-risk metric.

Your City – A personalized dashboard showing local trends, pollution indicators, and plain-language explanations.

Compare Mode – Side-by-side comparisons of up to four cities.

Earth Detective Missions – Guided investigations that help users explore real environmental questions using NASA data.

AI Trend Assistant – Explains datasets, trends, and statistical results in simple language. All calculations are produced by deterministic statistical methods before AI-generated explanations are provided.

Plain Language Mode – Converts technical statistical terms into explanations that students and non-specialists can easily understand.

Impact

Environmental data is often available but difficult to interpret. Trend Detector helps bridge that gap by turning scientific observations into understandable, evidence-based insights.

Citizens can explore how environmental conditions in their city are changing.

Students can learn how scientists identify meaningful trends in real-world data.

Educators can use NASA observations to teach environmental science and data literacy.

Researchers and journalists can generate clear, exportable summaries backed by real data.

Most importantly, the platform helps users become Earth Data Detectives by encouraging exploration, critical thinking, and evidence-based conclusions.

Technology

Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet, Canvas

Backend: FastAPI, Node.js, NumPy, SciPy

Data Processing: Python, Pandas, NASA Earth observation datasets, automated validation workflows

AI: Groq (gpt-oss-120b) with deterministic statistical calculations and offline fallback support

What Makes It Creative

Trend Detector combines NASA Earth science, statistical analysis, and AI-assisted exploration into a single experience designed for non-experts.

Rather than showing raw datasets, it guides users from questions to evidence-based answers. Every result is backed by real observations, transparent methods, and clear uncertainty information.

The goal is not just to show data, but to help people understand environmental change and confidently interpret the evidence behind it.

Key Principles

• Real observational data, not synthetic data

• Transparent and statistically validated results

• Plain-language explanations for accessibility

• Clear communication of uncertainty and limitations

• User privacy and responsible data use

Vision

Our vision is to make NASA Earth science data accessible to everyone. By helping users discover what is changing, where it is changing, and whether those changes are significant, Trend Detector turns complex environmental observations into knowledge that people can understand and use.
